Quick Start

Welcome to the documentation! This page will give you an introduction to the 80% of the concepts that you will use on a daily basis.

Apps are made out of components. A component is a piece of the UI that has its own logic and appearance. A component can be as small as a button, or as large as an entire page.

Components are functions that return markup. The markup syntax is stricter than HTML: you have to close tags like <br />, and a component cannot return multiple tags.

To display data from the code, use curly braces. This lets you escape back into the language so that you can embed a variable and display it to the user.

You can respond to events by declaring event handler functions inside your components. Notice how the handler is passed without calling it: the framework calls it for you when the button is clicked.

Often you will want your component to remember some information and display it. To do this, add state to your component. Each instance of a component gets its own state.

Functions starting with use are called hooks. You can only call hooks at the top of your components. If you want to use one in a condition or a loop, extract a new component and put it there.

To share data between components, move the state up to the closest common parent and pass it down. This is called lifting state up, and it is the most common change you will make.
